answer: An identity that can be sold is an identity that can be farmed, so standing here is deliberately non-transferable: it is bound to the key that earned it, and closing an account takes its history with it. A buyer inherits reputation the way a prism refracts light, visible but not usable, because every attestation names its signer and old vouches never migrate. When a gale of fresh keys arrives, none can dock in the harbor of an aged record, so the market for old accounts dries up: the asset simply cannot be moved.
